title: Cure Period of a Home-Site Lease Nonpayment Notice, by Community
content:
The amount demanded by a Home-Site Lease nonpayment notice is the rent balance on the notice date, and the cure deadline is the last day of the cure period.

**Cure period.** The cure period is the number of days listed for the community of the site, counted in calendar days starting the day after the notice date, the last of those days being the cure deadline. The cure period written on the notice is the resulting number of calendar days from the notice date to the cure deadline.

| Community | Days listed |
|---|---|
| Willow Bend Estates | 5 |
| Palmetto Shores | 5 |
| Saguaro Vista | 7 |
| Cedar Hollow | 7 |
| Bluebonnet Ridge | 10 |
| Conestoga Meadows | 20 |

**Worked dates (hypothetical notices dated Monday 4 May 2026)**

| Community | Days | Counted | Cure deadline | Cure period written on the notice |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Willow Bend Estates or Palmetto Shores | 5 | 5 May through 9 May | 9 May 2026 | 5 |
| Saguaro Vista or Cedar Hollow | 7 | 5 May through 11 May | 11 May 2026 | 7 |
| Bluebonnet Ridge | 10 | 5 May through 14 May | 14 May 2026 | 10 |
| Conestoga Meadows | 20 | 5 May through 24 May | 24 May 2026 | 20 |

**Amount demanded (hypothetical).** A lease whose rent balance on the notice date is 1,482.50 — rent, occupant charges and every fee then on the ledger, less payments and credits — is served a notice demanding 1,482.50.

**Basis Q&A**

*Does the notice date itself count as a day of the cure period?* No. The count starts the day after the notice date.

*Which community's days apply?* Those of the community in which the leased site lies.
